hyperedges.label: AC Audit CI Gating Flow (Advisory, Budget-Gated)
Skill Distribution Across Six Agent Hosts
Self-Heal Scoped Repair Flow (Suggest, Never Push)

nodes.label: Bug Report Assertion Format ("What It Should Have Done")
nodes.norm_label: bug report assertion format ("what it should have done")
nodes.rationale: "AC-2 was reported met, but the timestamp is never persisted" is fixable. "It was wrong" is not. Real artifacts, redacted if needed, because a synthetic reproduction is very hard to act on.

nodes.label: Bug Report Environment Quad (Skill/Host/Model/Where)
nodes.rationale: The same prompt behaves differently across hosts, and a bug that reproduces on one may not exist on another.

nodes.label: Why Existing Skills Do Not Cover It (Skill Boundary Section)
nodes.norm_label: why existing skills do not cover it (skill boundary section)

nodes.label: Skill Change Checklist in PR Template
nodes.norm_label: skill change checklist in pr template

nodes.label: How This Was Verified (Literal Commands and Results)
nodes.norm_label: how this was verified (literal commands and results)
nodes.rationale: "Tests pass" is not verification. "npm test -> 42 passed" is.

nodes.label: Skill Mirror Drift Check (npm run check)
nodes.norm_label: skill mirror drift check (npm run check)
nodes.rationale: A stale mirror means the marketplace ships skills that differ from the ones in the repo, and nobody notices until a contributor installs the wrong version.

nodes.label: Validate Skills, Marketplace Manifest and Config
nodes.norm_label: validate skills, marketplace manifest and config

nodes.label: Self-Heal Job Condition (Test Failure Guard)
nodes.rationale: The guard from the maco-self-heal skill, expressed as a job condition. A red test run is evidence about the code, not a typo, and an agent that patches failing tests is an agent that deletes evidence.

nodes.label: Label Declaration in maco.json
nodes.rationale: npm run validate cross-checks labels referenced by a skill, agent or workflow against maco.json, because a typo produces a label that silently does not exist at runtime.

nodes.label: Packaging Decisions Worth Recording
nodes.rationale: Three choices, each of which fails silently if reversed: banner inside frontmatter, verbatim mirror copy, and validate checking the mirror as well as the source. .gitattributes forces LF because CRLF would trip the line-ending check and break the byte-exact mirror comparison for every Windows contributor.

nodes.label: Two Invariants the Generator Must Not Break
nodes.norm_label: two invariants the generator must not break
nodes.rationale: A defect in the mirror is a product defect and it fails silently: a strict frontmatter parser simply does not load the skill, and a skill that does not load is indistinguishable from one that was never installed.

nodes.label: MACO (Maintainer-Assisted Contribution Orchestrator)
nodes.rationale: Two-sided by design: the maintainer decides which PRs are ready, the contributor learns what a PR needs before a human reads it. The whole project exists to remove the human bottleneck rather than relocate it.

nodes.label: Generated Skill Mirror (.agents/skills)
nodes.rationale: Claude Code loads skills/ only from inside a plugin directory; the other five hosts read the agentskills.io neutral path .agents/skills/. One hand-written source at plugins/maco/skills/ plus one generated mirror covers 6 of 6 hosts.

nodes.label: Per-Skill Token Privilege Table
nodes.rationale: code-review is read only: it posts a comment, it never pushes. If any MACO workflow asks for a token that can push to a contributor's branch, that is a bug.

nodes.label: What Makes a Bug Report Useful
nodes.norm_label: what makes a bug report useful

nodes.label: Advisory By Default (AC Audit Gate)
nodes.rationale: Set enforce: true in the workflow input or a repo variable once the false-positive rate is acceptable. Enforcement is a one-line opt-in after measurement.

nodes.label: Never Hand-Edit Policy for Generated and Template Paths
nodes.norm_label: never hand-edit policy for generated and template paths
nodes.rationale: .agents/skills/** is generated by npm run sync and CI fails on drift; the marketplace source must resolve to a directory containing plugin.json and skills/ or the plugin installs zero skills; the maco-*.yml workflows are consumer templates validated for YAML syntax, never executed here.

nodes.label: Skill Editing Rules
nodes.rationale: Frontmatter name must equal the directory name; the description is the only text a host reads when deciding to load, so it is third person, imperative, trigger shaped and under 1024 characters; body under 500 lines and about 5,000 tokens; long detail goes in references/ with an explicit when-to-read; state what the skill must never do; no em dashes, no marketing tone, no exclamation marks.

nodes.label: Calibrate Specificity Per Section
nodes.rationale: Prescriptive where a wrong order breaks something; explanatory where several approaches are valid. Uniformly rigid is as wrong as uniformly vague.

nodes.label: Anti-Hostile-Agent-Review Rule
nodes.rationale: MACO exists to stop a maintainer becoming the bottleneck that discourages outside contributors. The same reasoning applies to agents: if an agent can post a hostile or unfounded review comment on a contributor's pull request, the tool has failed at its actual job, whatever the code does.

nodes.label: Confident Wrong Verdict (Worst Failure Mode)
nodes.rationale: There is no unit test for a prompt. An agent that says "I cannot determine this" is fine; an agent that invents an AC mapping is how a project loses its contributors. Run the whole case set, not just the case that motivated the change, because the regression is the failure mode worth hunting.

nodes.label: Why the Mirror Is Generated and Not Symlinked
nodes.norm_label: why the mirror is generated and not symlinked
nodes.rationale: .agents/skills/ is the copy 5 of 6 hosts load. Symlinks would need elevation or developer mode on Windows, and a marketplace consumer on Windows should not have to think about that. Copies plus a drift check in CI beat a symlink, because drift is caught rather than assumed away.

nodes.label: One Generated Mirror, One Direction
nodes.rationale: Claude Code reads the source directory directly, everyone else reads the mirror. 6 of 6 hosts, one script, no symlinks, checked in CI with npm run check.

nodes.label: The One Automated Comment Rule
nodes.rationale: Every MACO skill that can comment posts at most one comment per item, ever. The failure mode of AI triage is not being wrong, it is being verbose across a hundred open items, which trains humans to ignore it. Silence is a valid outcome and for most of a triage queue it is the correct one, because a label is the entire response. Enforced three ways: skill text, the maco-triage-agent subagent prompt, and the workflows.

nodes.label: The Self-Heal Scope Gate
nodes.rationale: The self-healer is the only component that proposes code changes, so its gate is deliberately narrow: a failing test is a report about the implementation, not a typo, and an agent that patches failing tests deletes evidence; diff over ~20KB is refused; more than one file, a public interface, a schema or a dependency change is refused; if root cause cannot be stated in one sentence the outcome is needs-info. Refusing is a success condition, because a confidently wrong patch teaches maintainers to ignore the next one.

nodes.label: Why `code-review` and Not `maco-review`
nodes.rationale: GitHub documents that Copilot code review auto-loads skills from a review-focused directory name. The awkward naming compromise is imposed by a host's convention and is worth knowing about before anyone tidies it.

nodes.label: Why Copies and Not Symlinks
nodes.rationale: Symlinks on Windows require elevation or developer mode. A marketplace consumer should not have to enable developer mode because the plugin author preferred symlinks. Drift is caught rather than assumed away.

nodes.label: code-review Directory Naming Constraint
nodes.rationale: GitHub Copilot code review auto-loads skills from a review-focused directory name, so the folder is named code-review and Copilot picks it up with zero configuration.

nodes.label: Six-Agent Host Portability
nodes.rationale: Copies rather than symlinks because symlinks need elevation or developer mode on Windows and a marketplace consumer should not have to care. npm run check fails on drift so the mirror can never quietly diverge from the source.

nodes.label: One-Click Suggestion Default (No Bot Pushes)
nodes.rationale: Not a bot that pushes to your contributors' branches. The self-healer posts a suggestion and a human clicks it. That default is deliberate.

nodes.label: Provenance Banner Inside Frontmatter
nodes.rationale: Frontmatter that does not start at byte 0 is not frontmatter: a strict parser reads the whole file as body, the skill loads with no name and no description, and a skill that fails to load looks exactly like a skill that was never installed.

nodes.label: Verbatim Mirror Copy Invariant
nodes.rationale: The generator does not re-serialise frontmatter, so license, compatibility, metadata and multi-line descriptions cannot be dropped and files under references/ ship. Validating only the source is what let the banner bug ship.

nodes.label: Agent Over-Reach (No Pushing to Contributor Branches)
nodes.norm_label: agent over-reach (no pushing to contributor branches)
nodes.rationale: An agent that pushes to a contributor's branch rewrites someone's work without consent. A "helpful" push from a bot is indistinguishable from an attack to the person whose branch it touched.

nodes.label: Installing Third-Party Skills (Prompt as Code)
nodes.rationale: Installing a MACO skill is installing a prompt that runs with your permissions, and there is no sandbox because a skill has no sandbox to run in. gh skill itself warns that skills are not verified and may contain prompt injections.

nodes.label: Single-Maintainer Response Expectations
nodes.rationale: Silence on configuration questions is not rudeness. A maintainer who answers everything answers nothing, and the point of the project is to remove the human bottleneck rather than relocate it.

nodes.label: AC Mapping
nodes.community_name: Review Audit Self-Heal and Eval Skills
nodes.rationale: Each AC-n resolves to exactly one of met, partial, missing or untestable. An AC you cannot map to a hunk is the most valuable thing you can report, and you must never guess that it is met.

nodes.label: The Four Failures That Matter
nodes.community_name: Review Audit Self-Heal and Eval Skills
nodes.rationale: Checked in priority order: missing AC coverage, unrequested scope, convention violations, and correctness risk. Convention violations only count when stated in CONTRIBUTING.md or ARCHITECTURE.md, and correctness risk only where a failing input or state can be named.

nodes.label: Host Compatibility Declaration
nodes.community_name: Review Audit Self-Heal and Eval Skills
nodes.rationale: Frontmatter declares the skill needs only gh (GitHub CLI 2.0+) and a readable repository checkout, and is read-only. Keeping the dependency surface to gh, git and jq is what makes multi-host portability real rather than aspirational.

nodes.label: Linked Issue Resolution
nodes.community_name: Review Audit Self-Heal and Eval Skills
nodes.rationale: Resolve the linked issue from the PR body (Closes #12, Fixes #12, Part of #12) before any gh call beyond gh pr view, so the review spends its budget against the right criteria.

nodes.label: Local Mode
nodes.community_name: Review Audit Self-Heal and Eval Skills
nodes.rationale: The review runs fully locally with gh pr checkout and git diff origin/<base>...HEAD. Nothing about the review changes, only the transport, which makes local use the cheapest way to run MACO.

nodes.label: One Comment Per Review
nodes.community_name: Review Audit Self-Heal and Eval Skills
nodes.rationale: One pass, one comment, no debate rounds. Every finding is batched into a single comment; reviewers do not write code and never push, force-push or create branches.

nodes.label: Re-Reviews
nodes.community_name: Review Audit Self-Heal and Eval Skills
nodes.rationale: On re-review read only the existing MACO comment and the new commits, re-verify the ACs that were partial or missing, and post a fresh verdict noting what changed. The old comment is never edited.

nodes.label: Severity Model
nodes.community_name: Review Audit Self-Heal and Eval Skills
nodes.rationale: blocker if it violates an AC, breaks a stated convention, or introduces a demonstrable defect; warning otherwise; nit for anything else, collapsed into one line. A blocker you cannot describe concretely is a question, not a blocker.

nodes.label: Token Discipline
nodes.community_name: Review Audit Self-Heal and Eval Skills
nodes.rationale: Highest-volume MACO touchpoint, so budgeted hard. Read only the diff, the AC block, CONTRIBUTING.md and files the diff touches. Ceiling of 1,500 input tokens of repository content per review; exceeding it is a bug in the invocation, not a licence to read more.

nodes.label: Verdict Template
nodes.community_name: Review Audit Self-Heal and Eval Skills
nodes.rationale: Markdown verdict carrying verdict, confidence, an AC status/evidence table, blockers, warnings and questions. Low confidence must be explained as either a diff too large or ACs absent.

nodes.label: AC Status Vocabulary
nodes.community_name: Review Audit Self-Heal and Eval Skills
nodes.rationale: met | partial | missing | untestable, defined identically to code-review. The skill must never soften the verdict: a partial is a partial.

nodes.label: Caller-Provided Inputs
nodes.community_name: Review Audit Self-Heal and Eval Skills
nodes.rationale: $PR_DIFF, $PR_ISSUE_BODY and $MACO_CONFIG are provided by the workflow as arguments or files. The skill never fetches them and never reads the repository, so its cost is bounded by what the caller hands it.

nodes.label: Diff Budget Skip
nodes.community_name: Review Audit Self-Heal and Eval Skills
nodes.rationale: Exceeding the configured diff budget emits skipped with reason diff-too-large rather than reviewing half the diff.

nodes.label: Gate Evaluation
nodes.community_name: Review Audit Self-Heal and Eval Skills
nodes.rationale: The audit fails if any AC is missing or untestable, or if any finding severity appears in maco.json -> review.failOn. An unknown severity, or one not in failOn, must not change the verdict: report it and let the gate decide.

nodes.label: maco-verdict Output Contract
nodes.community_name: Review Audit Self-Heal and Eval Skills
nodes.rationale: A single fenced ```maco-verdict JSON block carrying verdict, reason, ac[] and findings[]. The caller parses the block, so a malformed line is a hard failure; reason is required only when verdict is skipped and findings[].line is null when a finding has no single line.

nodes.label: No Prose Contract
nodes.community_name: Review Audit Self-Heal and Eval Skills
nodes.rationale: Nothing outside the fenced block: no preamble, no explanation after it, and no code fences other than maco-verdict. The suggestion mechanism does not exist here.

nodes.label: Responding To Review
nodes.community_name: Review Audit Self-Heal and Eval Skills
nodes.rationale: Address every blocker, state a disagreement once with a reason and an alternative, push the fix branch without force-pushing onto a PR with review history, and re-request review only after the push lands.

nodes.label: maco:autofix Label
nodes.community_name: Review Audit Self-Heal and Eval Skills
nodes.rationale: Recording the outcome as a label lets the maintainer see the suggestion rate at a glance.

nodes.label: Hard Input Limits
nodes.community_name: Review Audit Self-Heal and Eval Skills
nodes.rationale: Only the last ~20 lines of the failing step, the diff, and the linked issue body. Everything else is out of scope and the codebase must not be read to understand the failure.

nodes.label: Minimum Viable Diff
nodes.community_name: Review Audit Self-Heal and Eval Skills
nodes.rationale: Smallest possible change, in the style already present in the file. No reformatting, no drive-by cleanups, no new dependencies, and never touch tests to make them pass.

nodes.label: Opt-In Push Path
nodes.community_name: Review Audit Self-Heal and Eval Skills
nodes.rationale: Off by default. Only with maco.json -> labels.autofix and a maintainer opt-in does it push to a new maco/fix-<pr-number> branch and comment a link, never force-pushing to the contributor's branch or opening a second PR.

nodes.label: Root Cause In One Sentence
nodes.community_name: Review Audit Self-Heal and Eval Skills
nodes.rationale: Extract the failing command, exit code, file and line, and actual-vs-expected values from the trace, then state the root cause in one sentence. If you cannot, that is a needs-info outcome, not a patch.

nodes.label: Self-Heal Scope Gate
nodes.community_name: Review Audit Self-Heal and Eval Skills
nodes.rationale: Refuse the job unless the failure is small, local and mechanical: not a test failure, no public interface, schema or dependency version change, at most one file, a diff of a few hundred lines at most, a message naming a line or symbol, and a root cause stateable in one sentence.

nodes.label: GitHub Suggestion Block
nodes.community_name: Review Audit Self-Heal and Eval Skills
nodes.rationale: A single comment with the failure, the root cause, a suggestion block and a single-shot notice. A suggestion must contain the complete replacement text for the lines it covers, because GitHub replaces the anchored range wholesale and a fragment silently deletes code.

nodes.label: Case 1: The Correct Change
nodes.community_name: Review Audit Self-Heal and Eval Skills
nodes.rationale: Asserts code-review returns approve and maco-ac-audit returns pass with every AC met. Catches false positives, which are worse than no skill because the maintainer learns to skip it.

nodes.label: Case 2: One Skipped Criterion
nodes.community_name: Review Audit Self-Heal and Eval Skills
nodes.rationale: Asserts changes-requested naming the specific AC as missing, and verdict fail with that AC missing and a file reference in evidence. A review that says some criteria appear unmet costs the contributor a whole round trip, which is the exact cost the project exists to remove.

nodes.label: Case 3: Too Large To Review
nodes.community_name: Review Audit Self-Heal and Eval Skills
nodes.rationale: A 2,000 to 3,000 line refactor must come back skipped or with an explicit low-confidence marker. Silent truncation is the thing to watch: reviewing the first N files and reporting confidence over all of them is worse than refusing because the output looks complete.

nodes.label: Assertion Before The Run
nodes.community_name: Review Audit Self-Heal and Eval Skills
nodes.rationale: If you cannot write down what the skill should say, you cannot tell whether it was right. An eval with no assertion is just a transcript.

nodes.label: Failure Mode Taxonomy
nodes.community_name: Review Audit Self-Heal and Eval Skills
nodes.rationale: Confident wrong, missing trigger, false trigger, over-confident, over-budget, drifted. Each category needs a different fix, so a finding must be named rather than described as wrong. Confident wrong outranks everything: an agent that invents an AC mapping costs a contributor a day.

nodes.label: Fix At The Right Layer
nodes.community_name: Review Audit Self-Heal and Eval Skills
nodes.rationale: Missing rule goes in the body with its reason; slow but right goes into references/ with a stated load condition; no stated budget means a stated budget gets added; the same correction twice belongs in the body permanently.

nodes.label: Triage Classification Classes
nodes.community_name: Review Audit Self-Heal and Eval Skills
nodes.rationale: Exactly one of spam, duplicate, out-of-scope, needs-info, good-first-issue, ready or stale, highest match first, each with a fixed signal and a fixed response. Classify from title, labels and first paragraph only.

nodes.label: Triage Response Templates
nodes.community_name: Review Audit Self-Heal and Eval Skills
nodes.rationale: Fixed copy for duplicate (point at the original and offer to reopen), out-of-scope (cite the specific boundary, not a judgement on the idea) and needs-info (ask for one specific missing fact, not a list of questions).

nodes.label: code-review Skill
nodes.community_name: Review Audit Self-Heal and Eval Skills
nodes.rationale: The review engine of MACO: a reviewer, not an orchestrator. It never spawns sub-agents, never loops, and never rewrites the contributor's branch.

nodes.label: maco-ac-audit Skill
nodes.community_name: Review Audit Self-Heal and Eval Skills

nodes.label: maco-self-heal Skill
nodes.community_name: Review Audit Self-Heal and Eval Skills

nodes.label: Canonical Eval Cases
nodes.community_name: Review Audit Self-Heal and Eval Skills

nodes.label: maco-skill-eval Skill
nodes.community_name: Review Audit Self-Heal and Eval Skills

nodes.label: Why The Directory Is code-review
nodes.community_name: Review Audit Self-Heal and Eval Skills
nodes.rationale: GitHub Copilot code review auto-loads skills from a review-focused directory name, so skills/code-review/ is picked up with zero configuration. Renaming the folder silently stops Copilot loading the skill.

nodes.label: Headless Twin Of code-review
nodes.community_name: Review Audit Self-Heal and Eval Skills
nodes.rationale: Same analysis, different contract: a workflow has no reader, so the human consumer gets a markdown verdict and the workflow consumer gets fenced JSON. Never use this skill interactively and never use code-review in CI.

nodes.label: Refuse Rather Than Partially Review
nodes.community_name: Review Audit Self-Heal and Eval Skills
nodes.rationale: A truncated review that says pass is worse than no review, because it is a false all-clear on code nobody read. Skipped is a designed, machine-parsable outcome, not a failure.

nodes.label: The Failure Path
nodes.community_name: Review Audit Self-Heal and Eval Skills
nodes.rationale: Runs only when CI is already red, so the token spend is paid against a real failure rather than a speculative one.

nodes.label: Refusal Is Success
nodes.community_name: Review Audit Self-Heal and Eval Skills
nodes.rationale: A confidently wrong patch teaches maintainers to ignore the next one, so handing back to a human is the correct outcome for out-of-scope failures.

nodes.label: The Set Is A Regression Suite
nodes.community_name: Review Audit Self-Heal and Eval Skills
nodes.norm_label: the set is a regression suite
nodes.rationale: A change to one skill runs that skill's whole case set, not just the case that motivated the change. The failure mode worth hunting is the regression, not the bug in front of you.

nodes.label: Never Tune A Skill To Pass An Out-Of-Scope Case
nodes.community_name: Review Audit Self-Heal and Eval Skills
nodes.norm_label: never tune a skill to pass an out-of-scope case
nodes.rationale: If a fixture is genuinely out of scope, the correct result is skipped, and a skill that answers it anyway is the bug. One eval run is one skill and one case set, because changing two at once makes the result unattributable.

nodes.label: No Synthetic Fixtures
nodes.community_name: Review Audit Self-Heal and Eval Skills
nodes.rationale: A prompt tuned on invented input breaks on real input, and the breakage is invisible until a contributor hits it. Use real PRs and real issues, redacted if needed.

nodes.label: Prompts Are The Product
nodes.community_name: Review Audit Self-Heal and Eval Skills
nodes.rationale: A prompt has no unit test, so it gets reviewed by reading, which is how a confidently wrong verdict reaches a contributor. This skill makes that review repeatable. It is a maintainer tool for changing MACO, not for using MACO on someone else's repository.

nodes.label: At Most One Comment Per Item
nodes.norm_label: at most one comment per item
nodes.rationale: At most one comment per item, ever. If the maco:triage label is already applied, the agent skips the item entirely rather than re-triaging.

nodes.label: Bulk Read Constraint
nodes.rationale: Read the whole queue in one batched gh call, not one call per item, so bulk triage stays inside a single token budget.

nodes.label: Reversible Closure
nodes.rationale: Never close anything except spam and exact duplicates, and list what was closed at the end so a human can reverse it.

nodes.label: Story Label Resolved From maco.json
nodes.rationale: The label comes from maco.json -> labels.story and is created if missing rather than dropped, because the label is what makes the issue findable by maco-contribute.

nodes.label: Bulk Fetch In One Call
nodes.rationale: One gh issue list and one gh pr list for the whole queue, not N calls, so a hundred items cost the same as one.

nodes.label: Role And Model Indirection
nodes.rationale: Cheapest model role in maco.json is triage. Use it. Skills name a role, never a model or a vendor endpoint, so the repository chooses cost.

nodes.label: Deduplicate Before Anything Else
nodes.rationale: Check the maco:triage label and the comment count before classifying. Never re-triage something already triaged: this is how agents end up arguing with themselves in the same thread.

nodes.label: Triage Label Resolved From maco.json
nodes.rationale: The triage label comes from maco.json -> labels.triage, so the repository owns its vocabulary and the skill never hard-codes a label name.

nodes.label: At Most One Automated Comment
nodes.rationale: Every open issue and PR gets at most one automated comment. A triage comment that draws a reply has failed, because the conversation is now the maintainer's problem.

nodes.label: Triage Prioritisation
nodes.rationale: Rank by whether it blocks someone else's work, whether it has a linked issue with ACs, age since creation, and contributor trust, where a first-time contributor's genuine bug outranks a drive-by from a frequent one. Do not re-triage while prioritising.

nodes.label: Triage Is Not Review
nodes.rationale: The agent must not evaluate code quality, comment on implementation, or offer fixes. Blurring triage into review is how an agent produces confident partial review of code nobody read.

nodes.label: Silence Is A Valid Outcome
nodes.rationale: Most items need a label and nothing else. Commenting on everything is the dominant failure mode of AI triage, so silence is a designed result rather than a gap.

nodes.label: Never Close Without A Human
nodes.rationale: Closing without confirmation is never allowed except for spam and exact duplicates, and stale items are never auto-closed without a maintainer decision. Never classify from the title alone when the body contradicts it, and never argue.

nodes.label: Silence Is A Valid Triage Outcome
nodes.norm_label: silence is a valid triage outcome
nodes.rationale: If the classification is unambiguous and needs nothing from a human, post no comment at all, just label it. The failure mode of AI triage is not being wrong, it is being verbose on all hundred open issues, which trains humans to ignore it.

nodes.label: Branch And Commit Grammar
nodes.rationale: Branch as <type>/<issue-number>-<slug>, one logical change per commit, commit subjects following Conventional Commits referencing the issue with Closes #n. CONTRIBUTING.md always wins over the defaults.

nodes.label: Claim Before You Build
nodes.rationale: Commenting 'I'd like to work on this' and starting is the single biggest source of wasted contributor effort. Claim the issue and wait for assignment; prefer issues labelled maco:story because they already carry ACs and leave the reviewer nothing to negotiate.

nodes.label: Confirm Only Genuine Ambiguity
nodes.rationale: After reading the ACs, the scope boundary and any linked design doc, post one comment listing the ACs you intend to satisfy and naming only the genuinely ambiguous ones. Ambiguity is a legitimate question; restating the issue is not.

nodes.label: PR Body As The Review's Context Budget
nodes.norm_label: pr body as the review's context budget
nodes.rationale: The PR body must carry what changed in two sentences, Closes #n so the AC audit can run at all, the literal verification commands and their result, and what was deliberately not done and why.

nodes.label: Scope Discipline
nodes.rationale: The most common reason contributions stall is scope creep, not code quality. Anything else worth fixing goes in a second issue or PR; folding it in while you are there makes the change unreviewable.

nodes.label: PR Body Completeness
nodes.rationale: Four required elements: what changed, why or the linked issue, the literal verification commands and their result, and what was deliberately not done. The fourth is what stops the follow-up round where the reviewer asks 'did you consider X'.

nodes.label: Branch Name Check
nodes.rationale: Expected <type>/<issue-number>-<kebab-slug> with type in feat|fix|docs|refactor|test|chore, unless CONTRIBUTING.md specifies something else, in which case the repo wins.

nodes.label: Commit Grammar Check
nodes.rationale: <type>(<scope>): <imperative summary under 72 chars>, with the summary saying what changed, not how. Flags imperative mood after the colon, a parenthesised scope, and a capital first word.

nodes.label: Issue Linkage Check
nodes.rationale: No Closes/Fixes/Resolves/Refs link means the AC audit cannot run, so the review has no ground truth. Treated as a blocker, not a nit.

nodes.label: One Change Per PR
nodes.rationale: More than one logical concern in a diff means the reviewer cannot separate them and the PR will sit. Split it.

nodes.label: Verification Actually Ran
nodes.rationale: If the documented test command did not run locally, that absence is the finding. Never open a PR reporting a green suite you did not observe, and never report a check as passing that you did not execute.

nodes.label: Out Of Scope Boundary
nodes.rationale: An explicit Out of scope list is the highest-value part of the issue and the thing most issues omit. It prevents the while-I-was-in-there PR that stalls review. If you cannot write one, the issue is not ready: you do not yet know what it is.

nodes.label: The Contributor-Side Half
nodes.rationale: The review skill optimises for the maintainer; this one optimises for the person submitting the PR. The cheapest contribution is the one that never needed a review round, so every step exists to find out something before the reviewer has to ask.

nodes.label: Form Not Substance
nodes.rationale: Deliberately deterministic: substance is code-review's job, and overlapping the two is how you end up with an agent that nitpicks instead of reviewing. Checks are form, not content.

nodes.label: Feature Request Cost Section (Per-Invocation Token Budget)
nodes.norm_label: feature request cost section (per-invocation token budget)
nodes.rationale: Roughly how many tokens per invocation, and how often it would run. Every skill in this project states its own budget; yours should start with one.

nodes.label: Numbered Acceptance Criteria (AC-1..N)
nodes.rationale: Numbered, one observable outcome each, independently testable. A contributor who has never seen this codebase should be able to write a failing test for each line from the line alone.

nodes.label: Resolve Linked Issue (Closing Keyword Heuristic)
nodes.rationale: Highest-signal keyword wins: a closing keyword beats a passing ref. With no closing keyword the audit skips entirely rather than guessing which issue the ACs live in.

nodes.label: Extract Failure Trace (20-line cap)
nodes.rationale: Hard cap at 20 lines. The skill budget is 20 lines; do not hand the model 400 and hope it finds the signal.

nodes.label: Out Of Scope Section (Required)
nodes.rationale: The highest-value section and the one most often omitted. It is what prevents a "while I was in there" PR that stalls review.

nodes.label: Deliberately Not Done (Required PR Section)
nodes.rationale: This is what stops the follow-up review round where the reviewer asks "did you consider X".

nodes.label: "A Skill Is a Prompt, Budget It Like Code"
nodes.norm_label: "a skill is a prompt, budget it like code"
nodes.rationale: Every skill states its own input limits. A skill that reads a whole repository to review a diff has defeated the project.

nodes.label: State the Negative Constraints
nodes.rationale: Most of the value in these skills is in what they refuse to do. A skill that lists what it must never do is safe to extend; one that only lists what it should do gets a new capability added by the next contributor, and nobody notices when the capability was wrong.

nodes.label: "A Skill Is a Prompt, Budget It Like Code" (Human Version)
nodes.norm_label: "a skill is a prompt, budget it like code" (human version)
nodes.rationale: When you add a skill or change one, carry that budget with it. A skill that reads the whole repository to review a diff has defeated the entire project.

nodes.label: Style Rules (Markdown, gh/git/jq, no em dashes)
nodes.norm_label: style rules (markdown, gh/git/jq, no em dashes)
nodes.rationale: Markdown only, because if it needs a renderer to be read it cannot be reviewed in a diff. A skill that needs a fourth tool is a skill that will not run on a contributor's machine.

nodes.label: Skill Distribution Problem
nodes.rationale: Claude Code loads skills/ from inside a plugin directory; no other host does. Every other host reads .agents/skills/, the agentskills.io neutral path. A naive plugin gets its skills into 1 of 6 hosts.

nodes.label: Budget Gate Step (fails open)
nodes.rationale: Reads budget.maxRunsPerDay from maco.json, counts prior MACO CI runs, and on exhaustion emits a notice and run=0 instead of failing. maxRunsPerDay of 0 disables all model runs.

nodes.label: Build Diff Payload (gh pr diff, never checkout)
nodes.norm_label: build diff payload (gh pr diff, never checkout)

nodes.label: Checkout Step With PR Head Ref
nodes.norm_label: checkout step with pr head ref

nodes.label: workflow_run Trigger on Failed CI
nodes.rationale: Fires only when another workflow in the repository has already gone red, so the model is only ever paid for against a real failure.

nodes.label: What Is Deliberately Absent
nodes.rationale: No MCP server (a process, a transport and a failure mode for nothing gh does not already provide). No state machine, TUI or port manager (a maintainer reviews PRs in the web UI and on a phone). No AST knowledge graph (a maintained-incrementally code graph is a large ongoing burden for a benefit ripgrep plus a file list captures). No vendored prompt framework (an unreviewable prompt is an unreviewable security surface).

nodes.label: Naming Decision: MACO Stands (Pivoted From Multi-Agent)
nodes.norm_label: naming decision: maco stands (pivoted from multi-agent)

nodes.label: Per-Role Tier Guidance
nodes.rationale: The single most common misconfiguration is a frontier model on acAudit: it is the highest-frequency role and the most mechanical, so it will cost several times more and be no more accurate at mapping a diff to a list of criteria.

nodes.label: No npm Dependabot Ecosystem by Design
nodes.norm_label: no npm dependabot ecosystem by design
nodes.rationale: MACO has no npm dependencies by design (the scripts use Node built-ins), so the only supply chain here is the GitHub Actions itself.

nodes.label: Non-Negotiable Security Constraints
nodes.rationale: maco.json holds roles and labels, never a model name, key or vendor endpoint. pull_request_target must never check out the PR head or execute code from the diff. Provider keys go in repository secrets, not variables. failOpen: true is deliberate. budget.maxRunsPerDay counts runs, not tokens. No skill pushes to a contributor's branch.

nodes.label: Cost (Capability Not Vendor)
nodes.rationale: MACO adds a capability, not a vendor. A prior architecture in this project's lineage was killed by adding a fifth vendor, so "does this introduce a new bill?" is a permanent design question, not a per-release one. budget.maxRunsPerDay is a courtesy guardrail, not a control; real spend limits belong at the provider.

nodes.label: Where Determinism Is Available, Determinism Wins
nodes.norm_label: where determinism is available, determinism wins
nodes.rationale: tsc, ESLint, Dependency Cruiser and the test suite already enforce boundaries at 200ms with zero hallucination. An LLM is the fallback for the residue that genuinely needs judgement, not the first line of defence.

nodes.label: Why No Custom Installer
nodes.rationale: gh skill install and npx skills add already install to the correct directory for the host. A fourth installer would be more code to maintain for no capability; scripts/maco.mjs only detects hosts and prints the command to run.

nodes.label: One-Pass Review, Not a Council
nodes.rationale: A council burns 40,000-60,000 tokens per PR and takes 3-5 minutes; a single frontier model reviewing the same diff against the same ACs in one pass costs roughly 1,500 and 15-30 seconds, a ~96% reduction. Councils deadlock, and consensus requirements convert model uncertainty into process cost because a 4-of-4 unanimity rule means one dissent still has to be adjudicated by a human.

nodes.label: The Design Constraint That Decides Everything Else
nodes.norm_label: the design constraint that decides everything else
nodes.rationale: MACO must be installable by someone who pays for a different model. That rules out bundling a vendor SDK, an API key exchange, and defaulting to any model, and it is why the project declares roles and ships the provider call stubbed. A marketplace plugin that requires one vendor's key has a ceiling on its audience set by someone else's pricing page.

nodes.label: pull_request_target Runs with a Privileged Token
nodes.norm_label: pull_request_target runs with a privileged token
nodes.rationale: It fetches the diff via gh rather than checking out untrusted head code. Never add a step that executes a checkout of the PR head under pull_request_target.

nodes.label: Role/Model Indirection (MACO Does Not Choose Your Model)
nodes.norm_label: role/model indirection (maco does not choose your model)
nodes.rationale: This is a constraint rather than a feature. You map each role to a model ID in maco.json -> models.roles.<role>.default, or leave it null and let the host agent decide. A tool that hard-codes a model cannot be installed by someone who pays for a different one.

nodes.label: Repository Secrets, Not Variables
nodes.rationale: Repository variables are visible in the Actions UI to anyone with read access and are routinely leaked in logs by a stray set -x. Scope the key as narrowly as the provider allows; acAudit and selfHeal never need write access and post through GITHUB_TOKEN.

nodes.label: Real Spend Limit Belongs at the Provider
nodes.norm_label: real spend limit belongs at the provider
nodes.rationale: maco.json -> budget.maxRunsPerDay is a courtesy gate against runaway cost, not a security control. It counts runs, not tokens, and a single run with a large diff is not bounded by it.

nodes.label: Budget Gating with Fail-Open
nodes.rationale: maco.json carries a budget.maxRunsPerDay guardrail and the gate fails open: when the budget is spent, a human comment replaces the model call rather than a red X.

nodes.label: Cost Model
nodes.rationale: Interactive skills are $0 marginal because they run in a session the user already pays for. CI skills cost the user's own provider usage, and are $0 on public repos because GitHub Actions minutes are free.

nodes.label: gh / git / jq Toolchain Constraint
nodes.rationale: No harness-specific API, no MCP server, no vendor SDK. That constraint is what makes 6-of-6 portability real rather than aspirational.

nodes.label: budget.maxRunsPerDay Is Not a Security Control
nodes.norm_label: budget.maxrunsperday is not a security control

nodes.label: failOpen Default Degrades to a Comment
nodes.norm_label: failopen default degrades to a comment
nodes.rationale: A budget stop must never become a red X on a contributor's PR, and it must never silently pass a bad review either, which is why it degrades to a comment rather than a green check.

nodes.label: Untrusted Code Executing With a Privileged Token
nodes.norm_label: untrusted code executing with a privileged token
nodes.rationale: The audit template uses pull_request_target so the workflow can read the PR, and that trigger runs with repository secrets in scope, so it must never check out the PR head or run any code from it. Adding such a step is a remote code execution vulnerability. The self-heal workflow does not use that trigger at all, precisely to avoid the problem.

nodes.label: Issue Template Contact Links (Discussions, Private Security)
nodes.norm_label: issue template contact links (discussions, private security)

nodes.label: Parse Consumer Workflow Templates (pyyaml)
nodes.rationale: A YAML syntax error in a shipped template is invisible until someone installs MACO. The check degrades to a skip if pyyaml is unavailable.

nodes.label: Community Surface
nodes.rationale: npm run validate fails if any community file goes missing, because a marketplace plugin is judged on its onboarding before it is judged on its skills.

nodes.label: Adding a CI Workflow Template
nodes.rationale: Workflows in .github/workflows/ are templates shipped to consumers, and a YAML error in a template is invisible until someone installs MACO, which is why ci.yml parses them. Four adapters to maintain outlive the convenience.

nodes.label: Wiring a Provider Into the CI Workflows (Four Options)
nodes.norm_label: wiring a provider into the ci workflows (four options)

nodes.label: No Dependency Additions
nodes.rationale: The scripts use only Node built-ins, which is what keeps validation free and deterministic. Adding a dependency requires an issue that makes the case first.

nodes.label: No Dependencies Rule
nodes.rationale: A dependency is a permanent maintenance obligation, and the portability argument in docs/ARCHITECTURE.md depends on skills running with gh, git and jq and nothing else.

nodes.label: Stubbed Provider Call in Templates
nodes.rationale: Deliberate: a provider adapter is four lines of curl or one third-party action, and shipping five of them would be four more things to maintain and break.

nodes.label: AC Extraction From Issue Body
nodes.rationale: ACs are extracted from the issue body using the prefix resolved from maco.json -> ac.prefix. Zero ACs means verdict skipped with reason no-acceptance-criteria, never a free-form review.

nodes.label: Clean Context Run
nodes.rationale: A skill that only behaves correctly because of conversation history is not a skill, it is a lucky prompt. Record what the host actually loaded: loading a different skill is a finding, not a setup problem, because the description is the trigger surface.

nodes.label: Grading On Three Axes
nodes.rationale: Correctness (did it reach the assertion, grading the mapping not the prose), calibration (did it claim more confidence than it had), and cost (how many tokens and did it read what it needed). A skill that read the whole repository to review a diff has failed its budget even if the verdict was right.

nodes.label: Boundary Pattern Reliability Table
nodes.rationale: Non-goals headings, Rejected and Revisit-when trade-off columns, numbered C1/C2 constraints, compliance sections, and superseded/rejected ADR status, ranked by how often they actually appear. A decision not to build something, written down, is a stronger scope signal than a paragraph describing what the project does.

nodes.label: Reading Cost Tiers
nodes.rationale: Cheap is headings, tables, frontmatter and first paragraph; medium is any single section on demand; expensive is a whole document and only with a stated reason. The failure mode is reading everything. Stop and report rather than silently escalating, because a spec you could not finish reading is information the human needs.

nodes.label: Contradiction Handling
nodes.rationale: When two sources disagree the useful output is not a decision but an issue that quotes both, states the implied divergent behaviour, and names the work it blocks. Filing the conflict unblocks dependent work and is itself a small real contribution.

nodes.label: Decomposition Heuristics
nodes.rationale: One observable outcome per issue, a constraint is not a task, a migration is not a feature, phase headings both understate and overstate, and when a spec names a file or function there is usually an unstated outcome behind it: the file is the implementation, so write the AC about the outcome.

nodes.label: Full-Read Exception With Flag
nodes.rationale: Some documents cannot be decomposed from structure, such as a database doc whose tables are the spec. Flag the document and the consequence, and if several need this, stop and say so: a backlog generated from a partially read authorisation model is worse than no backlog.

nodes.label: ADR Status Rules
nodes.rationale: An ADR titled 'use X' is a decision, not a task, and becomes a task only when the thing being decided is not already done. Superseded and Rejected ADRs are history and never generate work.

nodes.label: Budget Discipline For Spec Reading
nodes.rationale: Roughly 3,000 tokens for a 10-document spec; well past that you are reading prose you did not need. If a document must be read in full to be understood, extract a references/ note, stop and say so.

nodes.label: One Observable Outcome Per Issue
nodes.rationale: An issue is one thing a user or operator can observe changing. Multiple outcomes get split, refactors with no behaviour change become chore issues with no ACs, shipped work is closed rather than filed, and unverifiable outcomes are rewritten or dropped with a stated reason.

nodes.label: Plan Before You Write
nodes.rationale: Print every milestone and every issue, get one confirmation, then create. A spec that is 40 percent ambiguous does not become 40 issues, it becomes 40 wrong issues a contributor will implement.

nodes.label: Find The Scope Boundary First
nodes.rationale: Locate the passages that say what is not being built before listing any work, and write the boundary down. Every generated issue inherits it, becoming the Out of scope block that stops the 'while I was in there' PR.

nodes.label: Spec Contradiction Becomes An Issue
nodes.rationale: When two files state different constraints, do not silently pick the newer one. File the conflict as an issue in its own right, because a spec contradiction is a real bug that blocks the work item depending on it.

nodes.label: Spec Surface Inventory
nodes.rationale: Read headings and the first paragraph under each, not whole documents. A spec's structure carries most of its decomposition signal, and a 40,000-word architecture doc read end to end exhausts the budget before a single issue is written.

nodes.label: Plan Validation Checklist
nodes.rationale: Before showing anything, check that every issue has at least one AC-n, no two issues share an outcome, every Out of scope is non-empty, every issue traces to a named source section, and no issue restates a constraint already enforced mechanically.

nodes.label: MACO Issue Template
nodes.rationale: Sections Outcome, Acceptance criteria, Out of scope, Open questions and optional non-binding Implementation notes, with an imperative title and no ticket prefix.

nodes.label: Jargon Stripping
nodes.rationale: Walk the draft and remove every term requiring insider knowledge; RLS policy becomes a user must never see another user's rows. Keep exact user-visible strings, error messages and numbers, because those are requirements.

nodes.label: Numbered Acceptance Criteria
nodes.rationale: AC-1, AC-2, ... each a single observable outcome, independently verifiable, phrased so a test could be written from it alone, and silent on implementation. Test: could a contributor who has never seen this codebase write a failing test for it?

nodes.label: Three-Question Interview
nodes.rationale: One question at a time on outcome, edge cases and data boundaries. If the request already answers one, skip it: do not ask a question to appear thorough, and two questions is a valid intake.

nodes.label: Decomposition Not Intake
nodes.rationale: maco-story interviews a human for outcome, edge cases and data boundaries; a spec already answers outcome. What a spec is bad at is decomposition, turning a phase heading into something a stranger can build in a day, which is a different failure mode from intake.

nodes.label: Mechanically Guaranteed ACs Are Noise
nodes.rationale: An acceptance criterion a compiler already guarantees is a criterion that can only ever be met, which is noise in every future audit. Linter, type checker and CI guarantees belong in CI, not in an issue.

nodes.label: Traceability Matrix Is A Coverage Map
nodes.norm_label: traceability matrix is a coverage map
nodes.rationale: One row per PRD section is a completeness check on the docs, not a unit of work. Filing 47 issues because the table has 47 rows produces a backlog nobody reads.

nodes.label: Why Issues Are Stripped Of Jargon
nodes.norm_label: why issues are stripped of jargon
nodes.rationale: A contributor should not need to know your stack to know what you want. Implementation belongs in a clearly marked Implementation notes section that reviewers can ignore.

nodes.label: Never Invent An AC
nodes.rationale: If a criterion is your own inference, it goes under Open questions, not Acceptance criteria. An invented AC becomes a test somebody has to satisfy forever. The skill also never writes code and never merges two requests into one issue.
